LanguageData.Dominion_WarGoal_Punitive_Desc: Teach them a lesson. If you win, their stability, legitimacy and economy suffer.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarGoal_Conquest_Desc: Take a settlement. If you win, it is ceded to the winner (to you as a vassal outpost through Faction Territories), or they pay instead.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarGoal_Vassalisation_Desc: Make them a puppet: it obeys, pays a little tribute, never attacks you and joins your wars.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarGoal_Tribute_Desc: They pay a large sum at the peace and tribute for 180 days after.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarGoal_RegimeChange_Desc: Overthrow their government. The new regime owes its position to the winner.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarGoal_Liberation_Desc: Free the settlements they have taken from others and return them to their owners.

LanguageData.Dominion_Terms_PlayerHumbled: {0} humiliates your government: you lose 30 influence.

LanguageData.Dominion_Blockade_SortieText: The garrison of {0} has sallied out to break your blockade. Fighters of {1} are attacking your caravan!
LanguageData.Dominion_Warband_InterceptActOfWar: Intercept the warband of {0} (an act of war)
LanguageData.Dominion_Warband_InterceptedText: Your caravan has fallen on a warband of {0}. Every one of them you defeat counts in the war.
LanguageData.Dominion_Warband_ApproachingText: A warband of {0} is marching on your colony and will arrive in about {1}. A caravan can try to intercept it on the way.

It moves with battles, occupations, blockades, deaths in combat, and slowly with the balance of strength and war weariness. 25 or more ahead sets the terms of a peace; far enough ahead, the loser capitulates.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarTab_NoWarbands: None in sight. You see the warbands of factions you have intel 25 or more on, and any near your colonies or caravans.
LanguageData.Dominion_CallToArms_NoWar: None of your enemies is one {0} could fight.
LanguageData.Dominion_CallToArms_Refused: {0} will not join your war against {1}.
LanguageData.Dominion_ColdWar_Disabled: Cold wars are switched off in the settings.
LanguageData.Dominion_ColdWar_Confirm: Declare a cold war on {0}? They will resent it, their spies will be busier in your colony, and their enemies will like you better. It is not war, but it can become one.

LanguageData.Dominion_Intercept_Ordered: {0} sets off after the {1}. The fight starts as soon as they catch up.

LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_Warbands_Desc: Factions at war send armies across the world map to besiege, blockade and raid, and to reinforce their allies.
LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_WarbandRaids_Desc: Factions at war with you may march warbands on your colony. They arrive as raids sized like any other. When off, warbands only fight each other.
LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_Occupation_Desc: Victorious warbands occupy enemy settlements. The peace decides whether they are kept.
LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_CapitulationScore_Desc: When one side of a war is this far ahead, the loser surrenders on the winner's terms. When you are involved, you are asked.
LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_JointWars_Desc: Factions at war ask their allies and puppets to join, you included.
LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_ColdWars_Desc: Bitter rivals of similar strength enter cold wars: arms races, propaganda, border skirmishes and proxy wars.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_IssueAdvisory_Desc:
Have a colonist go on the colony radio and talk everyone through the latest news: what it means, what it does not, and why there is no need to panic.
A colonist with research work enabled reads it at a radio receiver. If it lands (better with high Social), it clears moods from bad news and foreign propaganda, cheers people up, and for {0} days colonists shrug off new bad news. A clumsy advisory makes things a little worse.
Colonists currently upset by the news: {1}.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_AdvisoryQueued: Advisory queued. The next colonist free for research work will take it to the radio.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_AdvisoryDone: {PAWN_nameDef} went on the air with a colony advisory. It landed: {1} worried colonists calmed down, and bad news will not rattle anyone for {2} days.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_AdvisoryFailed: {PAWN_nameDef}'s radio advisory fell flat. If anything, people are more nervous now.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_Investigate_Desc:
Send the story to the radio desk. A colonist with research work enabled calls around on the radio (contacts, traders, other stations) until it is confirmed or exposed as false.
Success is likelier with high Intellectual and good radio coverage. An inconclusive result can be tried again. Exposing a false rumour runs a correction at once and clears the worry it caused.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_InvestigateNote: Unverified. Stamp it to have the radio desk check the story.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_InquiryNote: The radio desk is on it: {0} done.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_InvestigateTrue: {PAWN_nameDef} checked the rumour on the radio. It is true: "{1}"
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_InvestigateFalse: {PAWN_nameDef} exposed a false rumour over the radio: "{1}". A correction is going out.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_InvestigateInconclusive: {PAWN_nameDef} could not get a straight answer on the radio about "{1}". It can be tried again.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_ReportAdvisory: reading a colony advisory on the radio.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_ReportInvestigate: chasing a rumour on the radio.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_WarUs: We are part of this. Check the War tab, keep the walls manned and the hospital beds made.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_WarAlly: An ally is involved and may call on us for help. The War tab shows how it is going.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_WarNear: The fighting is close. Expect more raiders, refugees and nervous traders around us.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_WarFar: Far enough away not to worry about, for now.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_EconomyDown: {0}'s economy is running at {1} of normal: their traders will have less to sell and want more for it.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_EconomyOk: {0}'s economy is holding up for now.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_Crisis: {0} is in crisis for about another {1}.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_Unstable: {0} is unstable ({1}/100). Unstable neighbours raid more and keep fewer promises.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_Espionage: Someone is playing games in the dark. The Intelligence tab shows how exposed we are.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_Peace: Trade along their routes should pick up again.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_Mood: This will rattle the colony ({0}). A colony advisory on the radio can calm people down.
LanguageData.Dominion_Advice_MoodShielded: A colony advisory is in force, so nobody will lose sleep over it.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_Order_Advisory_Desc: A calm, sensible talk through the latest news. If it lands (Social), it clears moods from bad news and foreign propaganda, everyone feels reassured (+3), and for 2 days new bad news does not upset anyone. A clumsy one makes people a little more nervous (-1).
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_Order_Morale_Desc: An hour of music, bad jokes and the weather. Quick, and it never fails: everyone gets a small lift (+2 for a day). It does not touch moods from bad news.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_Order_CounterPropaganda_D: Answer the pamphlets and whispers from abroad. If it lands (Social), foreign propaganda moods are cleared and enemy propaganda gets no hold on the colony for 5 days.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_Order_Investigate_Desc: Call around on the radio (contacts, traders, other stations) until the rumour is confirmed or exposed as false. Slow; success is likelier with high Intellectual and good radio coverage, and an inconclusive result can be retried. Exposing a false rumour runs a correction at once and clears the worry it caused.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_Order_Debunk_Desc: Declare the rumour false on air, without checking. Quick. If it really was false, a correction runs and the worry goes. If it was true, the colony feels lied to (-3 for 2 days) and the story stands confirmed.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_Order_Spread_Desc: Make sure everyone hears the good news, and hears it often. Everyone gets a lift (+3 for a day).
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_Order_Suppress_Desc: Quietly make sure this story is not repeated. Quick: the mood it caused is cleared at once. But there is a 1 in 4 chance word gets out that it was hushed up (-2 for a day).
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_Queued: Sent to the radio desk: {0}. The next colonist free for research work will take it.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_NoStory: The story is no longer in the paper.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_StoryBusy: The radio desk is already working on this story.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_NotBadNews: only for news that upsets the colony
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_MoraleDone: {PAWN_nameDef} spun some records and told some jokes on the colony radio. Spirits are up.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_CounterFailed: {PAWN_nameDef}'s counter-propaganda broadcast fell flat. The pamphlets keep circulating.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_CounterDone: {PAWN_nameDef} took the foreign propaganda apart on air. It will get no hold on the colony for {1} days.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_DebunkRight: {PAWN_nameDef} called it a lie on air, and it was: "{1}". A correction is going out.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_DebunkWrong: {PAWN_nameDef} called it a lie on air, but it was true: "{1}". The colony feels misled.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_SpreadDone: {PAWN_nameDef} made sure everyone heard the good news: "{1}".
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_SuppressDone: {PAWN_nameDef} kept "{1}" off the colony radio. Nobody is talking about it any more.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_SuppressLeaked: {PAWN_nameDef} tried to keep "{1}" quiet, but word got out that it was hushed up.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_AdvisoryMenu_Desc: Choose a colony advisory for the radio desk: keep calm, a morale broadcast, or counter-propaganda. A colonist with research work enabled reads it at a radio receiver.\n\nColonists currently upset by the news: {0}.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_RespondMenu_Desc: Choose what the radio desk does about this story: investigate or debunk a rumour, spread good news, or keep bad news off the air. Only what applies to the story is offered.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_OrderNote: Radio desk: {0}, {1} done. Press the stamp to cancel.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_RespondNoneNote: Nothing the radio desk can do fits this story: only rumours can be investigated or debunked, only good news spread, and only news that upset your colonists kept off the air. Open the stamp to see each option.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_RespondNote: The radio desk can respond to this story: {0}.
LanguageData.Dominion_Radio_NoStories: No recent story the radio desk can act on
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_NewsCategory: Show only stories from one desk (war, diplomacy, economy...). Choose "All" to see every story.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_NewsFaction: Show only stories about one faction.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_ShowRumors: Include unconfirmed rumours. Rumours may be false; the radio desk can investigate them.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_UnreadOnly: Show only stories you have not opened yet.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_MarkAllRead: Mark every story as read (removes the red pins).
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_Clipping: Click to read the full story.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_Ticker: The latest story to reach the colony. Click to open it in the newspaper.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_PlanOp: Plan a covert operation against a faction: choose the operation, the target and how your agents go in.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_ShowTarget: Jump to the objective or your agents on the map.

LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_ProposeMotion: Put a motion on the council's agenda. Members vote on it at the next session.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_Proclaim: Proclaim the planetary federation. This is the end of the Dominion story for this colony.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_ShowOnMap: Jump to it on the world map.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_SelectFaction: Click to see {0}'s details and what you can do with them.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tip_CancelTreaty: Cancel this treaty. The other side will not be pleased, and it may count as breaking your word.
LanguageData.Dominion_Setting_WarbandSpeed_Desc: How fast warbands march across the world map. At 1x a warband covers a tile an hour; the default 2x is half an hour a tile.
LanguageData.Dominion_Warband_Won: {0}'s warband beat your caravan. War score +{1} for them.
